chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
When you are behind an Imam and he recites al-Ḥamd and finishes its recitation, then say: “You are the praise, for Allah, Lord of the worlds,” and do not say: “Āmīn.”

key_terms.آمِينَ: the phrase prohibited here from being said after al-Ḥamd in this context
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْحَمْدَ: Sūrat al-Ḥamd, the Opening chapter recited in salat (prayer)
key_terms.رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: Lord of the worlds, part of the Quranic phrase cited in the supplication
key_terms.قِرَاءَتِهَا: its recitation, referring to the recitation of al-Ḥamd

ai.seo_question: What should a follower say after the Imam finishes al-Ḥamd in congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal instruction concerning what should be said in congregational salat (prayer) after the Imam completes Sūrat al-Ḥamd. It indicates that one should not say “Āmīn” after al-Ḥamd, reflecting a specific ruling in Shia fiqh regarding prayer recitation etiquette.
